recipe.description: You plucked a single berry or wild fruit from the cluster.
recipe.tip: Mixed berry patches ripen unevenly — separate them one at a time to sort each fruit.

recipe.description: You strained the mashed berries to separate the smooth pulp from the seeds and skins.
recipe.tip: Strain smashed soft fruits to extract pure pulps and juices.

recipe.description: You sorted a single ripe fruit from the wild harvest.
recipe.tip: Mixed fruit baskets hide surprises — separate them one at a time to learn what you have.

recipe.description: You drew off a distinct kind of water from the wild source.
recipe.tip: Water looks uniform until you separate it — spring, mineral, rain, and sea each behave differently in the pot.

recipe.description: You unearthed a single edible root from the tangle below.
recipe.tip: Root patches hide many species — separate them carefully one at a time.

recipe.description: You dug up one starchy tuber or wild root from the mound.
recipe.tip: Tuber piles look alike underground — separate them to sort each variety.

recipe.description: You cracked out a single nut from the wild harvest.
recipe.tip: Mixed nuts rattle together — separate them one shell at a time.

recipe.description: You picked out one fungus from the foraged cluster.
recipe.tip: Never rush a mushroom basket — separate and identify each find one at a time.

recipe.description: You threshed out a single grain from the wild grasses.
recipe.tip: A handful of grasses holds many cereals — separate them stalk by stalk.

recipe.description: You clipped a single tender shoot from the bundle.
recipe.tip: Young shoots look alike at a glance — separate them gently one by one.

recipe.description: You sorted a single seed type from the dried harvest.
recipe.tip: Seed sacks hold mixtures — separate them to learn what will sprout or roast.

recipe.description: You pulled one shellfish from the tidepool catch.
recipe.tip: Mixed shore harvests need sorting — separate each creature carefully.

recipe.description: You crushed the potato into a rough, starchy mash.
recipe.tip: Smash starchy tubers to break down fibers before mixing or cooking.

recipe.description: The apple blistered and darkened over open heat.
recipe.tip: Char fruit over flame to deepen sweetness before finishing a dish.

recipe.description: Steam and radiant ground heat slow-caramelized the sweet potato inside the earth pit.
recipe.tip: Pit-cook sweet potatoes in an Earth & Dirt Oven for ultimate tenderness.

recipe.description: Aromatic hardwood smoke cured and deeply flavored the fish.
recipe.tip: Cure and smoke cleaned fish using the Smoke & Cure technique.

recipe.description: The shellfish opened up, tenderly steamed by wet earth and stone heat.
recipe.tip: Bake shellfish in a dirt fire pit to steam them naturally in their shells.

recipe.description: You crushed and ground the wheat berries into fine, powdery flour.
recipe.tip: Grind or pound wheat to make raw flour.

recipe.description: The flatbread blistered and puffed rapidly on the scorching stone hearth floor.
recipe.tip: Bake raw dough directly on the floor of a Hearth & Clay Oven.

recipe.description: You laid the dough directly onto the glowing wood coals. It puffed up, covered in clean grey ash.
recipe.tip: Bake dough directly in hot ashes to make a primitive ash cake.

recipe.description: You crushed and ground the almonds until they released their oils, forming a thick paste.
recipe.tip: Grind or pound almonds to release fats and form almond paste.

recipe.description: The seeds popped and smelled beautifully of roasted oils.
recipe.tip: Toast sunflower seeds over open flame or coals.

recipe.description: The shrimp turned a brilliant pink, steamed perfectly by hot rocks in the earth oven.
recipe.tip: Bake shrimp under hot rocks in an earth pit oven.

recipe.description: Sizzling hot stones dropped into the water, bringing the soup to a bubbling boil until the vegetables turned sweet and soft.
recipe.tip: Boil the raw stew pot with hot stones or stovetop heat.

recipe.description: You scraped away the thin outer skin of the ginger.
recipe.tip: Use the peel technique to prep fibrous roots before cutting.

recipe.description: You cut the peeled ginger into paper-thin matchstick julienne.
recipe.tip: Julienne aromatics to release their flavorful oils rapidly.

recipe.description: You shredded the green onion shoots into fine julienne curls.
recipe.tip: Use knife skills on fresh scallions to prep them for flash cooking.

recipe.description: You pressed the dry seeds, extracting their pure golden oil.
recipe.tip: Apply pressure to oilseeds or nuts to extract cooking oil.

recipe.description: You crushed and pressed the nuts, extracting a rich oil.
recipe.tip: Apply pressure to oily nuts to extract cooking oil.

recipe.description: The oil heated until it shimmered and sent up faint wisps of smoke.
recipe.tip: Apply heat to cooking oil to prepare it for high-temperature searing.

recipe.description: You cleanly scaled, gutted, and scored the fish.
recipe.tip: Use the fillet skill to scale and clean whole fish.

recipe.description: Steam rose around the fish, cooking it until the flesh turned tender and flaky.
recipe.tip: Steam prepared fish using a controlled stovetop boil/simmer.

recipe.description: You fermented the seeds, brewing a dark, savory liquid.
recipe.tip: Ferment seeds to brew soy sauce.

recipe.description: You led one animal out of the herd.
recipe.tip: Herds gather together — separate them to milk, shear, or butcher each animal.

recipe.description: You obtained chicken meat and a fresh egg.
recipe.tip: Separate the chicken to obtain meat and an egg.

recipe.description: You obtained duck meat and a fresh egg.
recipe.tip: Separate the duck to obtain meat and an egg.

recipe.description: You obtained fresh beef and a pail of milk from the cow.
recipe.tip: Separate the cow to obtain both beef and milk.

recipe.description: You obtained pork from the pig.
recipe.tip: Separate the pig to obtain pork.

recipe.description: You gathered one ripe item from the wild patch.
recipe.tip: Wild flora patches hold various herbs and crops — separate them to sort cabbage, tomato, onion, eggplant, chili, citrus, and basil.

recipe.description: You carefully extracted sweet honey from the nest.
recipe.tip: Wild hives hold liquid honey — separate them carefully to avoid bee stings.

recipe.description: You mixed flour and water, kneading them into a smooth, elastic dough ball.
recipe.tip: Combine flour and water to form dough, then knead it to strengthen structure.

recipe.description: You placed the roots, wild mushrooms, and water together in a cooking vessel.
recipe.tip: Combine water, carrots, and mushrooms to prepare a raw stew pot.

recipe.description: The seeds swelled and split, sending out pale shoots.
recipe.tip: Soak seeds in fresh water to coax them into sprouting.

recipe.description: Berries and spring water mingled into a fragrant brew.
recipe.tip: Combine ripe berries with clean spring water for a simple restorative drink.

recipe.description: Sprouted seeds broke down into a mellow, drinkable tonic.
recipe.tip: Blend sprouted seeds with spring water for a filling camp drink.

recipe.description: Mash and charred fruit came together into a smoky-sweet hearth dish.
recipe.tip: Fold charred fruit into mash for a finished fireside plate.

recipe.description: Carrot and water simmered into a clear, sweet broth.
recipe.tip: Steep a root vegetable in spring water for a quick broth.

recipe.description: Mash and water loosened into a simple, filling stew.
recipe.tip: Thin mashed tubers with spring water for a quick stew.

recipe.description: You arranged the cleaned fish on a platter with ginger and scallions.
recipe.tip: Combine prepped fish with julienned aromatics before cooking.

recipe.description: You splashed the shimmering hot oil over the fish, followed by soy sauce. The kitchen filled with a magnificent aroma.
recipe.tip: Splash hot oil and soy sauce onto cooked steamed fish for a spectacular finish.
